clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive NBIA caused by FA2H variants, usually presenting in school-age childhood.
FA2H mutations produce an allelic spectrum spanning FAHN, hereditary spastic paraplegia SPG35 and a leukodystrophy, with overlapping and sometimes coexisting features.
The core phenotype is progressive spastic quadriparesis with cerebellar ataxia, dystonia and dysarthria.
Early optic atrophy with falling visual acuity and oculomotor abnormalities (nystagmus, strabismus) is common.
Seizures and progressive cognitive decline tend to emerge later in the course.

A distinctive MRI combination points to the diagnosis: white-matter signal change (hypomyelinating/leukodystrophic), progressive pontocerebellar atrophy with a thin corpus callosum, and globus pallidus iron on iron-sensitive sequences.
FA2H encodes fatty acid 2-hydroxylase, which hydroxylates fatty acids used to build myelin sphingolipids, so FAHN is fundamentally a myelin-lipid disorder with secondary iron accumulation.
reference.pathophysiology: FA2H, located on chromosome 16, encodes fatty acid 2-hydroxylase, an endoplasmic reticulum enzyme that introduces a hydroxyl group at the 2-carbon of free fatty acids to generate 2-hydroxy fatty acids. These 2-hydroxylated species are incorporated into the galactolipids of myelin, notably galactosylceramide and sulfatide, where they stabilise the lipid bilayer and maintain the long-term integrity of the myelin sheath. Loss of enzyme activity yields structurally abnormal, unstable myelin, driving progressive demyelination and hypomyelination, secondary degeneration of long white-matter tracts and cerebellar pathways, and eventual iron accumulation in the globus pallidus that brings the disorder within the NBIA family. Because the same enzyme deficiency can manifest predominantly as spasticity (SPG35), as a leukodystrophy, or as the full FAHN syndrome, the phenotype forms a continuous allelic spectrum, and inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: Other NBIA subtypes (PKAN, MPAN, BPAN, PLA2G6-associated neurodegeneration)
Leukodystrophies (metachromatic leukodystrophy, Krabbe disease, hypomyelinating leukodystrophies including Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease)
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI with iron-sensitive sequences to identify pallidal iron alongside white-matter change, pontocerebellar atrophy and a thin corpus callosum
FA2H testing within an NBIA, leukodystrophy or hereditary spastic paraplegia gene panel
Ophthalmological assessment with optical coherence tomography and visual evoked potentials for optic atrophy
Nerve conduction studies where a peripheral neuropathy is suspected
Leukodystrophy metabolic screen to exclude treatable mimics (for example arylsulfatase A, galactocerebrosidase and very-long-chain fatty acids)
EEG if seizures occur, and neuropsychological assessment
redFlags: Rapid loss of ambulation or new swallowing difficulty with aspiration risk
reference.prognosis: FAHN is progressive, with most affected children losing independent ambulation during adolescence and developing severe disability; life expectancy is reduced, often into early adulthood. Care is supportive and multidisciplinary.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosis as cerebral palsy because of early spasticity, which delays genetic testing.
Focusing on either the leukodystrophy or the pallidal iron in isolation, when it is their combination that suggests FAHN.
Not recognising the FA2H allelic spectrum, so that pure SPG35 presentations are not connected to FAHN.
Settling on the diagnosis before excluding treatable leukodystrophy mimics.
references: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) clinical references
management: Manage spasticity with antispasticity agents such as baclofen or tizanidine, botulinum toxin for focal tone, and physiotherapy with orthoses to preserve mobility
Treat dystonia with agents such as anticholinergics or a trial of levodopa, using botulinum toxin for focal dystonia
Control seizures with antiseizure medication as they emerge
Provide low-vision support for progressive optic atrophy and speech, communication and swallowing support for dysarthria and bulbar decline
Offer neuropsychological support and assistive technology for progressive cognitive decline
Coordinate multidisciplinary neurology, rehabilitation, ophthalmology and palliative care
Provide genetic counselling and family testing given autosomal recessive FA2H inheritance
